newsitem.title: USA: Handex Corp to sell environmental unit.
newsitem.headline: Handex Corp to sell environmental unit.

text.p: Handex Corp said on Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to sell its environmental unit to a corporation formed by an investment group which included members of its southeast regional management team, for about $21 million.

Proceeds from the sale and from retained assets would be about $21 million after recognizing a $7.3 million loss on the sale, for the writeoff of goodwill, establishment of valuation reserves and transaction costs, the company said.
The sale, subject to stockholder approval, was scheduled to be completed by the end of 1996, Handex said.
Under the agreement, the group would buy the stock of Handex's environmental subsidiaries for cash and other consideration, including a promissory note and preferred stock, the company said.
Proceeds from the sale would fund both internal growth and future acquisitions, the company said.

Handex, which had provided both educational and environmental services, said the deal was part of a strategic initiative to concentrate resources in the faster growing computer education and training industry. It participates in this area through its New Horizons Education Corp subsidiary.
Upon closing of the deal, the Handex name would be transferred to the buying group and the company's name would probably be changed to a variation of "New Horizons," it said.

Its environmental business had net operating revenues of $46.5 million and net income of $450,000 for 1995, and net operating revenues of $33.3 million and a net loss of $135,000 for the first nine months of 1996, Handex said.

The subsidiaries being sold operated out of 18 locations in 14 states, predominantly in the eastern half of the United States, Handex said. They provide environmental remediation services mostly at retail gasoline stations, it said.
